Oral Order

This criminal miscellaneous case arises out of a petition under Section 482 of the CrPC, filed by the accused persons, principally against the State of Bihar and O.P. No. 2, being the informant, with a prayer to quash the criminal proceeding instituted upon Complaint Case No. 344(C) of 2016 under Sections 498A, 354, and 323 of the IPC, and the order of cognizance thereof taken by the learned jurisdictional Magistrate on 30th May, 2016.
2.
It is not in dispute that the marriage of O.P. No. 2 Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.31230 of 2016(11) dt.05-08-2025 was solemnized with petitioner no. 1 on 08th December, 2010.

Petitioners no. 2 and 3 are her parents-in-law, and petitioners no. 4 and 5 are her brother-in-law and his wife,
respectively.
At the outset, shorn of unnecessary details, it is necessary to state the complainant's case.
It is stated by the complainant that after the solemnization of marriage, she went to her matrimonial home and, a few days thereafter, moved to Ghaziabad, where her husband used to work.
There, she lived with her brother-in-law and devrani (sister-in-law).

sentences.text: It is alleged that O.P. No. 2 was subjected to cruelty by the accused persons on account of a demand for a motorcycle from her parents.
Her brother-in-law and his wife allegedly assaulted her to compel fulfillment of the unlawful demand.
On 25th December, 2015, they allegedly assaulted her in the presence of her husband and attempted to strangulate her.
She was saved by neighbors who rushed in upon hearing her cries for help.
5. Thereafter, she left her matrimonial home with her minor daughter, aged about four years at the relevant time, and returned to her paternal home on 23rd December, 2016.
Subsequently, the accused persons allegedly came to her parental house, abused her brother, and threatened him with dire Patna High Court CR.
MISC. No.31230 of 2016(11) dt.05-08-2025 consequences.

The said complaint is annexed with the instant petition as Annexure-5.
6.
The learned Advocate on behalf of the petitioners submits that O.P. No. 2 used to quarrel with her husband at Ghaziabad without any rhyme or reason.

The husband of O.P. No. 2, along with his brother, his brother's wife, and petitioners no. 2 and 3, submitted an informatory petition before the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Darbhanga, against O.P. No. 2, her parents, and others, wherein it was stated that within eight months of marriage, the complainant had left her matrimonial home on 8th July, 2011, along with her ornaments, clothes, and other articles.

7. The petitioner no. 1 being the husband of the O.P. No. 2 lodged a complaint before the Special Superintendent of Police, Ghaziabad, stating, inter alia that his wife was abusing and threatening him saying that she would put entire family members of the petitioner no. 1 in a criminal case by committing suicide and also threaten him that she would take away the only daughter of the parties.

Again on 22 nd February, 2016, the petitioner no. 1 lodged another complaint before the SSP,
Gautam Budha Nagar, stating, inter alia, that his wife along with her brother and two other unknown persons left his Patna High Court CR.
MISC. No.31230 of 2016(11) dt.05-08-2025 residential flat at Ghaziabad with their minor daughter.
8. On careful perusal of the chain of evidence as depicted in various documents annexed by the petitioners, it appears that within few months of marriage, family discord started between the parties.
The father of the petitioner no. 1 (petitioner no. 2 herein) made a complaint before the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Darbhanga that the opposite party no. 2 left her matrimonial home.
The learned Advocate on behalf of the petitioners refers to an order passed by the learned Principal Judge, Family Court, Gautam Budha Nagar on 18.12.2017.
On perusal of which it is found that the application under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act was decided on compromise.

It was settled between the parties that the petitioner no. 1 would behave properly with the opposite party,
he would not abuse her, nor will commit any "
  
" with the opposite party.
Both parties will respect each other and will perform their obligations as husband and wife respectively.
Thus, on such terms, the case under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act for restitution of conjugal right was compromised.

It appears from the compromise decree that the husband of the petitioner/wife did not behave properly with the opposite party/wife and he used to commit "
  
" with the Opposite Party No. 2.

It is needless to Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.31230 of 2016(11)
dt.05-08-2025 say that mental abuse and physical assault are components of cruelty when it is associated with an allegation of demand of a motor-cycle.

The complaint filed by the O.P. No. 2 Prashant Kumar And Ors vs State Of Bihar And Anr on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190626082/
2 clearly described the role of the petitioners no. 4 and 5 in the complaint.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: They tried to strangulate the opposite party no. 2.

The role of the father-in-law of the O.P. No. 2 is also attributable to the incident of cruelty because he made out a false case against the O.P. No. 2 by filing an informatory petition before the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate that the O.P. No. 2 left her matrimonial house with her ornaments and other belongings on 08 th July 2011.
The said fact is prima facie false.
The husband of the O.P. No. 2 stated that she stayed with him at Ghaziabad during the year 2015 to 2016.
9. The learned Advocate on behalf of the O.P. No. 2 has raised all the above-mentioned contradictions in the case from the materials on record.
10. It is no longer res integra that Section 482 of the CrPC is to be used very sparingly.

There are only three grounds where Section 482 of the CrPC is applicable, viz., to make orders as may be necessary to give effect to any order under the Code or to prevent the process of abuse of any Court or otherwise to secure the ends of justice, in addition to the Patna High Court CR.
MISC. No.31230 of 2016(11) dt.05-08-2025 statutory provision

, let me now quote the circumstances stated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335 where an FIR /complaint and the order of cognizance can be quashed.

entities.text: Haryana v. Bhajan Lal, 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The parameters are as follows:
"(1) Where the allegations made in the first information report or the complaint, even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety do not prima facie constitute any offence or make out a case against the accused.
(2) Where the allegations in the first information report and other materials, if any,
accompanying the FIR do not disclose a cognizable offence, justifying an investigation by police officers under Section 156(1) of the Code except under an order of a Magistrate within the purview of Section 155(2) of the Code.
(3) Where the uncontroverted allegations made in the FIR or complaint and the evidence collected in support of the same do not disclose the commission of any offence and make out a case against the accused.
Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.31230 of 2016(11) dt.05-08-2025 (4) Where, the allegations in the FIR do not constitute a cognizable offence but constitute only a non- cognizable offence, no investigation is permitted by a police officer without an order of a Magistrate as contemplated under Section 155(2) of the Code.
(5) Where the allegations made in the FIR or complaint are so absurd and inherently improbable on the basis of which no prudent person can ever reach a just conclusion that there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.
(6) Where there is an express legal bar engrafted in any of the provisions of the Code or the concerned Act (under which a criminal proceeding is instituted) to the institution and continuance Prashant Kumar And Ors vs State Of Bihar And Anr on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190626082/
3 of the proceedings and/or where there is a specific provision in the Code or the concerned Act,
providing efficacious redress for the grievance of the aggrieved party.

entities.text: Prashant Kumar And Ors vs State Of Bihar And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (7) Where a criminal proceeding is manifestly attended with mala fide and/or where the proceeding is maliciously instituted with an Patna High Court CR.
MISC. No.31230 of 2016(11) dt.05-08-2025 ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance on the accused and with a view to spite him due to private and personal grudge."

11. I do not find suppression of any of the above parameters in the instant proceeding under Section 482 of the CrPC accordingly, the instant miscellaneous case being devoid of any merit is dismissed on contest.
There shall, however, be no order as to cost.

(Bibek Chaudhuri, J) Suraj Dubey/-
